description: Earliest known concept/build in the Alfr3d lineage.
Early 2014 iteration of the home-automation daemon.
2014 iteration, ordering relative to MK-I/MK-II unconfirmed.
Home-automation daemon running on a Pi (/home/alfr3d/alfr3ddaemon.py), audio handling.
Added Python LIFX integration (pylifx).
Server + mobile companion apps split out: Alfr3dServer, Alfr3d4Android-Original, Alfr3d-MKIII-Android, alfr3d.io.
Separate repo from the 2015 MK-IV Notion page, not yet reconciled with it.
First Kafka message-bus architecture (topics speak/environment/device/user); direct architectural precursor to today's Kafka-based backend. Undated.
Repo explicitly describes itself as "Successor to Project Alfr3d" — a rebrand attempt that didn't end up replacing it. Undated.

Now Littl3-1-Engineering/alfr3d, 534 commits on main, latest tagged release v0.2.0. Described by its own README as "the final resting place of Alfr3d after years of different architectures and repos."
Product site for Littl3.1 Engineering with Alfr3d as flagship. Pages: index.html, alfr3d.html, lab.html.

Containerized microservices (Kafka, MySQL, Redis, FastAPI, React), Nexus/Domain/Matrix frontends, Spotify integration, RTSP/HLS camera streaming (now device-registry-backed, multi-camera), WHEN/IF/THEN automations, situational-awareness engine, IoT sync across Home Assistant/SmartThings/ESPHome. Tagged v0.2.0 "Multi-Camera Registry", 2026-08-21.

Free spatial launcher + $5.99 Pro unlock live, CI builds debug APK on every push to main, signed-release workflow on version tags. Latest tag v0.1.29; a rotation-lock setting bumped the code to v0.1.30 (not yet tag-cut).

User-defined Primary/Action/Environmental accent colors via an in-app HSV picker, sharing the same palette-derivation code as the wallpaper-inferred theme. Backgrounds/glass/text stay fixed for legibility. Also fixed a hardcoded radial-menu wedge color bug for the launcher category on the two data-driven theme variants.

New "Lock screen rotation" toggle in Behavior settings — launcher stays upright portrait regardless of device orientation when enabled; follows system auto-rotate when disabled (default). Verified on-device in both directions. Bumped to v0.1.30 in code; not yet tag-cut (latest tag v0.1.29).
Core free / Nexus Launcher free+$5.99 Pro / Cloud Phase 3 $5.99-$11.99 / Kit unscheduled, published on littl31.com/alfr3d.html.
All 3 repos (alfr3d, alfr3d_deck, Littl31) migrated from personal armageddion account to the Littl3-1-Engineering org.

Remote-access relay (no port forwarding) + push notifications; "thin, dumb-pipe relay" that never sees plaintext data. Now scoped into a phased plan in todo_cloud_relay.md: architecture spike -> subscriber/billing identity + Stripe -> relay/tunnel -> FCM push -> security review. Deliberately a separate identity system from household RBAC auth. Not yet built.

Both tags now cut. v0.1.8 "Situational Awareness Registry" and v0.2.0 "Multi-Camera Registry" (adds ESPHome as a local-only IoT provider, moves camera streaming to a device-registry-backed multi-camera model, unifies version numbering across every service).

Signing, Gradle Play Publisher, and gated CI already wired up; blocked on manual account-holder steps: Play developer enrollment, Play Console app entry, first manual release upload, sensitive-permission declarations + demo video, hosted privacy policy URL, CI service account for future automated releases.
Pre-flashed Raspberry Pi appliance, built to order. Parked until Alfr3d Cloud proves demand. Not yet scheduled.

Corrected: repo does have a LICENSE file (FSL-1.1-ALv2 text, matches the site). GitHub's NOASSERTION was a license-detector classification gap for a non-SPDX-standard license, not a missing file. No action needed.
Push notifications to the launcher; depends on Alfr3d Cloud Phase 3 shipping first.
Its own todo/ folder was checked directly and contains only a completed bugfix note (mobile scramble jitter fix); no forward-looking roadmap items exist for the site itself.
JWT-based auth with a role-based ACL (technoking/resident/guest) gating all write routes; currently zero auth exists on any API route. Planning only, not started.
Attribute calendar/Gmail integrations to individual household members instead of one shared global account. Blocked on Auth + RBAC landing first.

Shipped in v0.2.0 (2026-08-21): mDNS discovery, Noise-encrypted native API, manual-accept flow for discovered nodes, runs always-on in parallel with whichever of HA/SmartThings is the default provider. Also fixed a pre-existing bug where /api/iot/devices only ever showed one provider's devices at a time. Phase 5 (persistent push-based state via subscribe_states(), replacing the 15-min poll) not started.

Every integration credential (ha_token, st_pat, Spotify client secret, ESPHome PSK) is currently plaintext in the config/smarthome_devices tables. Scoped as its own item after the ESPHome PSK design deliberately chose plaintext-for-v1. Planning only, not started.

milestone: Kit ordering / Cloud signup commerce plan
description: Phased plan to give the Kit and Cloud pricing sections a real path from visitor to paying customer — site currently has zero CTA/checkout links on either tier. Phase A: free waitlist/interest-capture forms. Phase B (gated on Kit waitlist signal): Stripe Checkout for the one-time Kit purchase. Phase C (gated on the Cloud relay being built): Stripe Checkout + Customer Portal + magic-link login alongside the relay's own subscriber identity. Planning only, not started.

Audit and bring pre-commit hooks, Dependabot, Aikido security scanning, and CI lint/test/build workflows to the same baseline across alfr3d, alfr3d_deck, and littl31 — alfr3d already has pre-commit + Dependabot + CI, the other two don't yet. Not started.
Init scripts (systemd unit or Docker restart policies) so all ALFR3D containers start automatically on host boot, without a manual docker compose up. Not started.

milestone: DB schema ER diagram for README/wiki
description: Export the current MySQL schema and generate an up-to-date ER diagram (e.g. Mermaid erDiagram) for the README and Notion wiki — the last diagram (if any) predates recent migrations (personality/context, IoT, routines). Not started.

Physical enclosure for the ALFR3D device + peripherals (mic/speaker/camera/sensors), matching the dark tactical/glassmorphic visual identity. Not currently scheduled — blocked on the hardware phase starting and a finalized bill of materials.

milestone: Personality ticks shouldn't fire on every speak
description: Personality quip "ticks" currently apply to every TTS speak action; should be probabilistic/occasional (random chance, cooldown, or context-based) so it doesn't feel like a bit every time. Newly scoped, not started.
Three parked options beyond the already-shipped HLS pipeline: WebRTC for sub-500ms latency, recorded/archived playback, and computer-vision motion/person detection.
Two more theme options for the existing theme-picker system, on top of the three already shipped (Cyan/Navy, Amber/Charcoal, Light/Teal).
Abstract audio-source interface so playback isn't Spotify-only — local library, Tidal, YouTube Music, radio — plus a loose future-ideas list (NLU voice control, Last.fm scrobbling, multi-room sync).

Daemon polls Spotify playback state, publishes change events, renders a situational-awareness card, exposes GET /api/music/now-playing. Code complete and unit-tested; not yet verified against a live Spotify-authorized deployment.
Have the launcher push on-device now-playing (any media session, not just Spotify) to the backend instead of only backend-side polling. Documented as a deferred fast-follow, not yet scoped.

Resolve Alfr3d's mood/genre recommendation into one specific real Spotify playlist and wire the launcher's ‘Play it’ button to deep-link into it. Implemented on both sides and passing unit tests; not yet verified on-device against a live deployment (backend and launcher todo files both cover this).
Personality panel currently shows call-count usage only; per-token usage metadata from the LLM client isn't surfaced yet. Minor — a future-enhancement aside, not a scoped plan.

Added real descriptive paragraphs to the Nexus Launcher, Core, Cloud, and Kit cards (plus a 4th intro-hero line). Also fixed a Locomotive Scroll init crash that was silently blocking all scroll-reveal content sitewide, a stale scroll-trigger-position bug after async image loads, and restructured card layout so text sits beside its screenshot instead of stacking below it.

bezier()'s returned easing closure read a module-scope C that was actually only declared inside runLogoAnimation()'s local scope, throwing ReferenceError whenever Snap invoked the easing function during the index-page splash logo animation. Hoisted config() to module scope to fix.
